flag.data: data folder: the accounts (accounts.json, holds tokens), the page key (key), the message log (messages.json), the tasks (tasks.json) and -background's log (bridge.log); SYMPHONY_DATA changes the default
flag.web: for development: serve the pages from this folder, so edits show after a reload; without it the built-in pages are used
flag.mod: for development: a mod folder that sessions started from the page get with --plugin-dir, overriding the installed copy; without it the mod installed in Claude Code is used
flag.terminal: ignored since 0.6: sessions started from the page run inside the bridge, and symphony attach <id> shows their terminal (kept so older -autostart entries still start)
flag.open: open the office in the default browser once the bridge is up; when a bridge already runs at -addr, just open its office
flag.autostart: on: start the bridge whenever you log in, with the flags given here, and start it now; off: undo that
flag.env_file: a file of variables to set when the bridge's own environment lacks them (-autostart on writes it: the bridge started at login gets only PATH)
flag.background: start the bridge in the background, detached from this terminal and logging to bridge.log in the data folder, and return once it answers
flag.stop: stop this data folder's bridge at -addr, however it was started (its sessions end), and return once it is gone
log.listening: symphony bridge {version}: {url}  (the office, signed in; approvals at /approve; data in {data})
log.already_running: a symphony bridge is already running at {url}
log.addr_taken: {addr} is taken: another program, or a symphony bridge with another data folder, answers there. Stop it, or give this bridge another address with -addr
log.data_in_use: the data folder {dir} is in use by its bridge at {url}; a bridge at another address needs a data folder of its own (-data)
log.data_locked: another symphony bridge is using the data folder {dir}; stop it, or give this bridge a data folder of its own with -data
log.addr_not_local: -addr {addr}: the bridge listens on this machine only; its host must be 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1 (as in 127.0.0.1:7788)
log.key_failed: can't read or make the page key in {dir}: {reason}
log.data_damaged: {file} is damaged ({reason}); the bridge can't start without it: restore it from a backup, or move it aside to start without what it holds
log.data_set_aside: {file} was damaged ({reason}); it was moved to {aside} and the bridge starts without it
log.key_unproven: {addr} doesn't prove it is the bridge with this page key (another program, a symphony bridge with another data folder, or an older one answers there), so the key isn't sent to it
log.stopped: stopped the symphony bridge at {addr}; its sessions have ended
log.stop_none: no symphony bridge with this data folder answers at {addr}: nothing to stop
log.stop_slow: asked the bridge at {addr} to stop, but it still answers after a minute (it may still be ending a task); try again later, or end its process
log.stop_forced: stopped by a second signal before the stop finished: the sessions were killed, and what was still being written or merged may be left as it was
log.push_failed: can't send the office page an update: {reason}
log.page_behind: an office page fell behind with its updates (a frozen or stalled tab); its stream was closed, and it reconnects for the whole state
log.task_undo_failed: task {task} didn't start, and some of what it made stays: {reason}
log.save_failed: can't write {file}: {reason}; until a write succeeds, what changed is in memory only
log.bot_home_no_git: git is not on PATH, so the employee's new folder {dir} isn't a git repository; install git (tasks need it too)
log.unsaved: stopping with data that couldn't be written to disk: {reason}
log.open_failed: couldn't open a browser ({reason}); open {url} yourself
log.autostart_on: symphony now starts when you log in ({where}); it's running at {url}
log.autostart_env: started at login, the bridge also gets {names} as this shell has them now (kept in {file}, which only you can read)
log.autostart_slow: symphony now starts when you log in ({where}), but doesn't answer at {url} yet
log.autostart_off: symphony no longer starts when you log in, and the bridge it started has stopped
log.autostart_off_window: symphony no longer starts when you log in; close the bridge's window to stop it now
log.autostart_off_quiet: symphony no longer starts when you log in
log.autostart_none: symphony wasn't set to start when you log in
log.env_file_failed: can't read the variables in {file} ({reason}); the bridge goes on without them (run symphony -autostart on again to write them anew)
log.autostart_go_run: -autostart needs the symphony program itself, not go run: download a release, or build it with go build -o symphony ./cmd/bridge
log.background: the symphony bridge runs in the background at {url}; its log: {log}
log.background_failed: the bridge stopped right after starting ({reason}); its log: {log}
log.background_slow: the bridge doesn't answer at {url} yet; its log: {log}
log.launch_off_mod: Starting sessions from the page is off: -mod {dir} is not a mod folder
log.launch_off_claude: Starting sessions from the page is off: {claude} not found
log.launch_on: Sessions started from the page run inside the bridge (nothing opens); symphony attach <id> shows one's terminal
log.mod_twice: mod: {id} is installed and enabled too: sessions started with -mod load both, so every hook runs twice (each event reported twice, two cards for one permission). While developing, turn it off: claude plugin disable {id}
log.mod_missing: mod: {reason}. To start sessions from the page, run: {fix} (no bridge restart needed)
page_key.title: Open the office from symphony
page_key.run: This page needs the bridge's key, which the symphony program hands to your browser. Run symphony again: it opens the office signed in.
page_key.log: Or open the address with the key (…/?key=…) that the bridge printed when it started: in its terminal, in bridge.log in its data folder, or, for a bridge started at login, in journalctl --user -u symphony on Linux and in ~/Library/Logs/symphony.log on macOS.
error.mod_check_failed: can't check whether the mod is installed (claude plugin list --json): {detail}
error.mod_not_installed: the symphony-bridge mod is not installed
error.mod_project_scope: the mod is only installed for one project ({scope}); install it at user scope
error.mod_disabled: the mod is installed but disabled
error.account_bad_name: a name needs 1 to 40 characters and no control characters
demo.flag.seconds: how long to run, in seconds; 0 runs until stopped
demo.flag.data: the bridge's data folder, where its page key is (key); SYMPHONY_DATA changes the default
demo.create_failed: {name}: can't create it (maybe it exists already): {error}
demo.not_enough: not enough demo accounts; delete the old demo accounts and run again
demo.no_key: can't read the bridge's page key ({reason}); give its data folder with -data
error.page_key: the bridge refused the page key: is -data the bridge's data folder?
attach.usage: usage: symphony attach [-addr host:port] [-data folder] <launch id>
attach.flag.data: the bridge's data folder, where its page key is (key); SYMPHONY_DATA changes the default, SYMPHONY_KEY gives the key itself
attach.no_key: can't attach: no page key for the bridge ({reason}); give its data folder with -data, or the key with SYMPHONY_KEY
attach.banner: symphony: {name}'s terminal. Ctrl-] or closing this window detaches; the session goes on.
attach.detached: symphony: detached from {name}; the session goes on.
task.kickoff.intro.lead: You are the lead of group {task}.
task.kickoff.intro.member: You are a member of group {task}; the lead is {lead}.
task.kickoff.intro.flat: You are a member of group {task}.
task.kickoff.title:
The user's task:

{title}
task.kickoff.untitled: The user hasn't described a task yet: they will say what to do in the group chat (it arrives as a message from the user). Until then, wait; don't start anything on your own.
task.kickoff.team:
Your team — Claude Code sessions on this machine; reach them with SendMessage by these names (they show in ListAgents):
{team}
task.kickoff.where.git: You are {name}: you work in your own git worktree {worktree} on branch {branch} of {dir} (base branch {base}); every teammate has a worktree and a branch of their own in their repository, so nobody steps on anyone's files.
task.kickoff.where.plain: You are {name}: you work in {dir} itself, the folder as it is (no branch or worktree of your own), so what you change is there at once. A teammate may work in the same folder: agree with them who edits which files, and don't check out, stash or reset the folder under them.
task.kickoff.rules.lead: Once you know what the user wants (the description above, or what they say in the group chat), break it down, give each teammate their part with SendMessage, answer their questions and review what they report. Split the work so that no two of you edit the same files. When they are done, tell the user what was done and what is left.
task.kickoff.rules.member: Wait for the lead's assignment (it arrives as a message), ask when something is unclear, don't edit files the lead gave to someone else, and tell the lead when you are done.
task.kickoff.rules.flat: Agree among yourselves with SendMessage who does what, so that no two of you edit the same files, and tell the user when you are done.
task.kickoff.git.lead: Commit your work to your branch. When the teammates are done, merge the branches of those who share your repository into yours (git merge <branch> in your worktree); branches in other repositories stay for the user. When the group is dissolved, the bridge commits what is uncommitted on every branch and removes the worktrees; if it made this repository for the group (the folder was no git repository before), it also merges the members' branches into {base}, otherwise the user merges your branch.
task.kickoff.git.member: Commit your work to your branch; when the group is dissolved, the bridge commits what is left uncommitted and removes the worktree.
task.kickoff.git.flat: Commit your work to your branch; when the group is dissolved, the bridge commits what is left uncommitted, removes the worktrees and may merge your branches into {base}.
task.joined: New in group {task}: {names}. Reach them with SendMessage by these names.
task.left: {name} left group {task}; don't send anything more to that name.
task.leadLeft: {name}, the lead, left group {task}: there is no lead now; agree among yourselves with SendMessage who does what.
